ba-are-we-fast-yet[bot] opened issue #15212:

are-we-fast-yet found 1 regression and 2 speedups in virtual cycles (callgrind) between Wasmtime 0eb6d77091c9 and 3e0ee3fbfdd8.

  • Baseline: run 00093 (metadata), Wasmtime 0eb6d77091c9
  • This run: run 00094 (metadata), Wasmtime 3e0ee3fbfdd8

A change counts when a Mann-Whitney U test finds it significant at the 0.01 level and it clears its phase's minimum relative change:

phase geomean individual
compilation 0.3% 1%
instantiation 2.5% 20%
execution 0.5% 2%

Regressions (1)

benchmark phase Δ virtual cycles virtual cycles noise Δ instructions retired instructions retired noise
cm-online-stats/cm-online-stats.wasm compilation +5.02% (+4.89% to +5.10%) 0.083% -> 0.167% +6.58% 0.104% -> 0.116%

Speedups (2)

benchmark phase Δ virtual cycles virtual cycles noise Δ instructions retired instructions retired noise
Geomean execution -1.82% (-1.88% to -1.77%) n/a n/a n/a
cm-online-stats/cm-online-stats.wasm execution -41.43% (-41.44% to -41.42%) 0.013% -> 0.016% -41.45% 0.003% -> 0.002%

A positive delta is a slowdown, a negative delta is a speedup.

instructions retired counts work done rather than how well it was predicted. A regression whose instructions didn't move is often Valgrind's branch predictors aliasing on a code layout change; see docs/regressions.md.

Each noise column is how far that event's own counts spread.

<details>
<summary>Other callgrind counters that changed for these benchmarks</summary>

benchmark phase counter Δ noise
cm-online-stats/cm-online-stats.wasm compilation data-reads +6.63% (+6.56% to +6.71%) 0.085% -> 0.100%
cm-online-stats/cm-online-stats.wasm compilation instructions-retired +6.59% (+6.49% to +6.69%) 0.104% -> 0.116%
cm-online-stats/cm-online-stats.wasm compilation indirect-branches +6.57% (+6.57% to +6.58%) 0.004% -> 0.009%
cm-online-stats/cm-online-stats.wasm compilation conditional-branches +6.18% (+6.02% to +6.34%) 0.169% -> 0.163%
cm-online-stats/cm-online-stats.wasm compilation indirect-branch-misses +5.89% (+5.88% to +5.90%) 0.016% -> 0.009%
cm-online-stats/cm-online-stats.wasm compilation data-writes +5.62% (+5.53% to +5.70%) 0.084% -> 0.125%
cm-online-stats/cm-online-stats.wasm compilation conditional-branch-misses +4.81% (+4.65% to +4.99%) 0.209% -> 0.230%
cm-online-stats/cm-online-stats.wasm compilation l1-dcache-read-misses +3.55% (+2.04% to +4.13%) 1.319% -> 1.727%
cm-online-stats/cm-online-stats.wasm compilation l1-dcache-write-misses +3.29% (+2.48% to +4.13%) 0.712% -> 1.080%
cm-online-stats/cm-online-stats.wasm compilation ll-dcache-write-misses +1.61% (+1.11% to +2.29%) 0.562% -> 1.032%

</details>

Commits

https://github.com/bytecodealliance/wasmtime/compare/0eb6d77091c930aa603b637bba4e1dbe5db2ddf8...3e0ee3fbfdd88d06c3f8c169168fe0d3b0c0096d

  • 3e0ee3fbfdd8 Inline to-owner borrow lends in sync-to-sync adapters (#15208)

Reproduce locally

On x86-64 Linux with Valgrind installed:

git clone https://github.com/bytecodealliance/sightglass
cd sightglass
git checkout 2d453335318d05cf42b6f3263aa68f0021985f10
rustc engines/wasmtime/build.rs -o build-engine
mkdir old new
REVISION=0eb6d77091c930aa603b637bba4e1dbe5db2ddf8 ./build-engine old
REVISION=3e0ee3fbfdd88d06c3f8c169168fe0d3b0c0096d ./build-engine new
cargo run --release -- benchmark --measure callgrind \
  --engine old/libengine.so --engine new/libengine.so \
  --engine-flags-common="-Cparallel-compilation=n --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu -Ccranelift-has-sse3 -Ccranelift-has-ssse3 -Ccranelift-has-sse41 -Ccranelift-has-sse42 -Ccranelift-has-popcnt -Ccranelift-has-avx -Ccranelift-has-avx2 -Ccranelift-has-fma -Ccranelift-has-bmi1 -Ccranelift-has-bmi2 -Ccranelift-has-lzcnt -Ccranelift-has-cmpxchg16b" \
  -- benchmarks/cm-online-stats/cm-online-stats.wasm

alexcrichton commented on issue #15212:

@fitzgen the regression here seems likely "there's more CLIF to compile", and given the purpose of it, you ok closing this?
